title: Connected geometric preimage of a purely inseparable singleton fibre
statement: Let $q:X\to T$ and $r:T\to U$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $p:X\to U$ satisfy $p=r\circ q$, and suppose $q$ is geometrically connected [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Let $u\in U$ and let $V\subseteq T$ be open. Suppose the open subscheme $V$ has exactly one point $v$ over $u$ and that its residue extension $\kappa(v)/\kappa(u)$ [def-weil-residue-field] is purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. Put $\Omega=\overline{\kappa(u)}$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. In the geometric fibre $X\times_U\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre] [def-pc-fibre-product], the inverse image of $q^{-1}(V)$ is connected and nonempty [def-weil-connected-scheme]. No properness, integrality, affine, finite-partition, or etaleness hypotheses are imposed.

proof.text: Put W = V.toScheme, f = V.ι ≫ r and a = W.fromSpecResidueField v. The composite a ≫ f factors as Spec of the given purely inseparable residue-field map followed by U.fromSpecResidueField (f v). The first factor is universally injective by lem-pc-spec-pure-insep-integral-radicial-surjective, and the second is a monomorphism. Hence a ≫ f is universally injective. For any singleton scheme Y → U mapping to f v, the base change of a ≫ f has at most one point. Pullback associativity identifies it with the pullback of a along pullback.fst f g. This latter projection surjects onto pullback f g: every point projects to v by fibre uniqueness, and Scheme.Pullback.exists_preimage_pullback lifts the pair consisting of this point and the residue-field point. Thus pullback f g has at most one point.

Take Y = Spec Ω and g the geometric point at u. Its point has image u = f v, so Scheme.Pullback.exists_preimage_pullback supplies a point z of pullback f g. Therefore pullback f g is a nonempty singleton. The pullback map j from this scheme into pullback r g has range equal to the inverse image of V under pullback.fst r g, by Scheme.Pullback.range_map and Scheme.Opens.range_ι. Consequently that inverse image is the singleton {j z}. No embedding of the residue extension into Ω is required.

The canonical map b : pullback (q ≫ r) g → pullback r g is a base change of q, by pullback pasting (IsPullback.of_bot), and hence is geometrically connected. The requested subset is b⁻¹({j z}) by the projection identity and the preceding range calculation. Mathlib Scheme.Hom.isConnected_preimage_singleton gives its connectedness, including nonemptiness. Substitute h to recover the specified structure morphism p.

theorem Scheme.Hom.isConnected_geometricFibre_preimage
    {X T U : Scheme.{u}} (q : X ⟶ T) [GeometricallyConnected q]
    (r : T ⟶ U) (p : X ⟶ U) (h : q ≫ r = p) (u : U) (V : T.Opens)
    (hv : ∃ v : V.toScheme, (V.ι ≫ r) v = u ∧
      (∀ w : V.toScheme, (V.ι ≫ r) w = u → w = v) ∧
      @IsPurelyInseparable (U.residueField ((V.ι ≫ r) v))
        (V.toScheme.residueField v) _ _ ((V.ι ≫ r).residueFieldMap v).hom.toAlgebra) :
    _root_.IsConnected
      ((pullback.fst p
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (algebraMap (U.residueField u) (AlgebraicClosure (U.residueField u)))) ≫
            U.fromSpecResidueField u)) ⁻¹' (q ⁻¹' (V : Set T)))
